tools.description: Apply insert/replace operations (max 50) to one file atomically. Targets are line ids ("12:a3") from view or edit output, verified before anything is written; a stale id fails with the current content. All targets refer to the original file and must not overlap. The result diff carries fresh ids for follow-up edits — no re-view needed; removed lines, and the middle of a long added block, show as an id range, and a trailing `shift:` line says how later original line numbers moved. Insert anchors 0 (file start) and -1 (end) are plain integers. Content is raw text without id prefixes.

content.description: Raw text to insert or replace with, no line-id prefixes.

end.description: `replace` only: last line to replace (inclusive), as a line id. Default: `start`.

start.description:
Line id in the ORIGINAL file: first line to replace, or the anchor to insert after
(for `insert` also the integers 0 = file start, -1 = after the last line).

tools.name: batch_edit
tools.title: Batch Edit

tools.description: Linux-only explicit same-size patch of at most 64 KiB, preserving inode/hard links/open-file identity. Requires expected version/hash, transaction ID and acknowledgement of NON-ATOMIC visibility. Durable private receipts support status/recovery. Optional special mode-bit preservation uses existing owner rights only. Not a transactional snapshot for concurrent readers; capabilities/immutable flags are refused.
tools.name: binary_patch_inode
tools.title: Recoverable Inode Patch

tools.description: Read bounded base64 file bytes with independent chunk SHA256 and next_offset. Pin expected_version from the first chunk. No 1 MiB total file limit.

expected_version.description: Bind every chunk to the version returned by the first read.

limit.description: Maximum returned bytes; capped at 64 KiB. Use next_offset until eof.

tools.name: binary_read
tools.title: binary_read

tools.description: Stage binary files in bounded chunks and commit only after total size and SHA256 verification. Retries are bound to upload ID and offsets; destination is unchanged until commit. Commit replay verifies the published destination; abort never deletes committed output. This does not lock out noncooperating writers.
tools.name: binary_upload
tools.title: binary_upload

tools.description: Atomically publish at most 1 MiB of decoded base64 under the target account. expected_version is mandatory; absent is create-only. Preserves supported descriptor-bound ownership/mode, xattrs and ACLs with verification; rejects hard-link splits and special execution flags before publication.

data_base64.description: Strict base64, up to 1 MiB decoded. Use binary_upload for larger files.

expected_version.description: Exactly the prior file version, or absent for a create-only write.

tools.name: binary_write
tools.title: binary_write

tools.description: Create a directory tree only inside the configured controller-local workspace. Existing directories succeed without change, while files or symlink components are refused. No command execution, remote host selection, privilege escalation or overwrite. Linux only.

path.description: Directory path in the configured local controller workspace. Remote paths are refused.

destination.description: Absent target directory path with an existing authorized parent.

source.description: Existing controller-local workspace directory, never a symlink or file.

tools.title: Move Workspace Directory Without Overwrite

tools.description: Read files, list directories, search content. Lines render as `N:hh|content`; copy `N:hh` verbatim — it is the line id edit tools target. Listings are recursive and gitignore-aware, one `path	NL	~Nt` (lines, ~tokens) per file. Re-viewing a whole file returns only the hunks changed since your last view (or an unchanged marker); ranged reads always return the requested lines. Reuse returned content: read a complete block in one call, combine adjacent windows, never re-read overlapping ranges or narrow one just to pick edit targets; re-read only when the file may have changed or output was truncated.

content.description:
Locate code: searches the whole file/tree (`start`/`end` ignored) for a literal
substring, or a Rust regex with `regex: true` (`(?i)` case-insensitive; alternation for
related terms).

end.description:
Last line (inclusive): line id or integer (negative counts from the end). Default: end
of file; omit both `start` and `end` for the whole file.

full.description:
Force the complete file when re-viewing a whole file (normally only changed hunks),
e.g. after losing earlier context. No effect on ranges or searches; output limits
unchanged.

max_depth.description:
Directory depth bound. Default: unlimited, except a bare remote listing (no
`pattern`/`content`) stops at the root entries. Searches walk the whole tree.

path.description:
File or directory. `a|b` searches several roots with `content` (max 32); several
files take parallel view calls. Remote: ssh://[user@]host[:port]/path (host may be an
~/.ssh/config alias; `ssh://host` or `ssh://host/~/dir` is the login home).

pattern.description:
Ripgrep -g globs bounding listings and searches: without `/` a name at any depth,
with `/` the relative path; `*`, `**`, `?`, `[abc]`, `{rs,toml}`, leading `!`; `|`
joins ordered globs (later wins), e.g. `**/*.rs|!target/**`. Applied after
gitignore/hidden filtering; one line, max 4096 bytes, 64 globs.

regex.description: Treat `content` as a regex. Default: false.

start.description:
First line (inclusive): line id or integer (negative counts from the end, -1 = last).
Default: line 1.
